1.explanation:
• src/js/components/Meter/README.md explains the Meter component’s intended behavior, props (including animation options), and examples.  
• src/js/components/Meter/index.js (or the main Meter source) contains the logic that computes the SVG path for the circle and applies the CSS transition to the <path> element. Inspecting it lets you see where the transition is set.  
• src/js/components/Meter/StyledMeter.js (or the styled-component wrapper) shows how the <path> is styled, including any default "transition: all 300ms" rules that trigger the glitch.  
• src/js/themes/base.js defines the default transition durations and easing used across components (including Meter). Overriding or removing the transition here is the primary way to reproduce or fix the Chrome-only animation issue.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot (and GIF) shows a circular Meter with a red arc representing a percentage value, a light gray background arc, and a numeric percentage (“44%”) centered inside. When the value changes in Chrome, the SVG <path> that draws the arc animates in an odd way—because of a blanket “transition: all 300ms” on the path—causing the stroke to redraw and distort before settling. In Firefox and Safari there is no animation, so the arc jumps directly to its new length without the strange intermediate effect.
